walkthrough:
Apply the binomial expansion formula to $(1 + 3x)^6$ in ascending powers of $x$:
$$(1 + 3x)^6 = 1^6 + \binom{6}{1} 1^5 (3x) + \binom{6}{2} 1^4 (3x)^2 + \dots$$

Evaluate the binomial coefficients and compute the powers:
$$1^6 = 1$$
$$\binom{6}{1}(3x) = 6(3x) = 18x$$
$$\binom{6}{2}(3x)^2 = 15(9x^2) = 135x^2$$

State the first three terms of the expansion:
$$1 + 18x + 135x^2$$

hints: Identify all products that produce an $x^2$ term: $1(135x^2)$, $-7x(18x)$, and $x^2(1)$.
walkthrough:
Write the product of the quadratic polynomial and the expansion from part (a):
$$(1 - 7x + x^2)(1 + 18x + 135x^2 + \dots)$$

Select the three products that contribute to the $x^2$ term:
$$1 \times 135x^2 = 135x^2$$
$$-7x \times 18x = -126x^2$$
$$x^2 \times 1 = 1x^2$$

Combine the coefficients to obtain the overall coefficient of $x^2$:
$$\text{Coefficient of } x^2 = 135 - 126 + 1 = 10$$
